title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Vitruvius paired shadows construct a meridian and offset streets from wind sectors
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. The source marks equal morning/afternoon shadows, constructs a north-south line, divides wind sectors, then directs streets between winds. A geometric construction produces a reference axis from two timed observations; a second derived partition controls permissible street direction. Sector names and boundary lines have different roles.

source.span: De architectura I.6.6-8, with I.6.12 diagram explanation as a separately declared continuation
source.observed_content: The source marks equal morning/afternoon shadows, constructs a north-south line, divides wind sectors, then directs streets between winds.
source.layer: Modern edition/translation of an ancient primary work; source-only exploratory input, not a newly collated medieval witness

potential_admitted_target: Already-admitted f67r1 or f57v geometry can be considered only after its fixed owner map is reviewed; no new target image or labels are requested.

design.mechanism: A geometric construction produces a reference axis from two timed observations; a second derived partition controls permissible street direction. Sector names and boundary lines have different roles.
design.unit: Complete I.6.6-8 construction and one complete admitted circular diagram/prose unit with independently fixed orientation.
design.contrast: A static wind list has no observation-to-axis dependence. Radial street alignment along the winds reverses the stated between-sector choice. Arbitrary rotation cannot rescue a fixed derived axis.
design.prediction: If a future reading owns morning and afternoon marks, it must derive a single consistent axis and preserve the offset between wind centres and street lines. A diagram that contains only sectors leaves this mechanism untested.
design.scope: Source-only raw proposal; no selected manuscript content, assigned glosses or executed experiment

Acquire a dated source diagram with separately captioned observation marks, meridian, winds and street boundaries.
Freeze target orientation from admissible visible evidence, then test both timed marks and the derived boundary relation; do not fit labels to compass directions.
